## Hypothesis history

- after step 12: Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.88, DNA damage 0.06, DNA replication 0.04, Eg5 inhibitors 0.01, Microtubule destabilizers 0.01

## Conclusion

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.88); key evidence e9, e5, e8, e2.

Why: Unanimous 4/4 NSC Aurora with saturated large-nucleus polyploidy and intact cytoskeleton agrees with protocol vote.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: DNA-content flow cytometry for polyploidy plus phospho-histone H3 and Aurora autophosphorylation immunofluorescence to confirm failed cytokinesis and target engagement.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

**Approve.** Aurora kinase inhibitors is strongly favoured over runner-ups: unanimous 4/4 NSC vote (summed similarity 2.815), 6/10 atlas neighbours for top class at ~0.72 mean vs DNA damage/DNA replication at ~0.50, and phenotype across all 4 wells (0.3-10µM) shows huge saturated polyploidy signal — frac_large_nucleus z≈+24 to +31 (27-35% vs 1.4% DMSO), nuc_area z≈+17-21, integrated DNA z≈+4-5, ~2× cell area — with microscopist reporting intact microtubules/F-actin, arguing against direct cytoskeletal/Eg5 classes (frac_mitotic_like=0). Effects are not a single weak well, and acquisitions spanned onset, bridging and high doses to discriminate. Flat dose-response (rho=-0.20) reflects saturation already at 0.3µM, not weakness. p=0.88 is calibrated given morphology/atlas cannot prove target alone. Budget is exhausted (0 left) and protocol_call is decisive and concordant, so no affordable experiment could change the call.

## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ-A** (no PubChem record shown)

Identity check: BBBC021 gives no structure for this compound (an internal code); name matches in PubChem would be unrelated compounds, so none is shown

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

The final call is the nearest-neighbour vote over the 4 wells the agent chose (4/4). The Scientist's own call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors** (agrees; right).

## Reflection

The Aurora kinase inhibitor call was correct, driven by an extreme saturated large-nucleus signal across all four wells: frac_large_nucleus z=+24.2 to +31.1 with nuc_area z=+17.2 to +20.6 and cell_area z=+17.1 to +28.6 from 0.3 to 10 uM, plus unanimous 4/4 NSC votes for Aurora kinase inhibitors and microscopist report of lower density with intact cytoskeleton (PMID 23468529).

The main misleading signals were the flat frac_large_nucleus dose-response (rho=-0.20, p=0.8) and persistent DNA damage/DNA replication k-neighbours (3/10 and 1/10 on the 4-well comparison). The acquisition choice to stop at 0.3 uM as the lowest dose missed the true onset because that well was already maximally saturated (z=+31.1), so flatness correctly reflected saturation rather than lack of activity, but threshold was never defined.

What was right:
- Prioritized large-nucleus polyploidy signal (frac_large_nucleus z=+24.2 at 1 uM and z=+28.9 at 10 uM) as discriminative for Aurora over cytoskeletal classes
- Used compare_to_reference_atlas early (2/2 Aurora) and again over 4 wells (4/4 Aurora, 6/10 k-neighbours) to confirm majority vote
- Used describe_phenotype visual check for intact microtubules/F-actin to downweight Eg5, microtubule and actin disruptors
- Interpreted flat dose-response as saturation already at 0.3 uM rather than evidence against Aurora

What was wrong or missed:
- Lowest acquisition at 0.3 uM was still saturated (frac_large_nucleus z=+31.1), so onset threshold to separate Aurora from DNA damage was not captured; should have acquired 0.01-0.1 uM wells
- Flat nuc_area dose-response (rho=+0.60, p=0.4) and flat frac_large_nucleus response (rho=-0.20, p=0.8) left dose-dependence unproven
- Second literature search for MCF-7 Aurora morphology returned 0 hits, providing no cell-type-specific support

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry for >4N polyploidy plus phospho-histone H3 and phospho-Aurora immunofluorescence to confirm failed cytokinesis and target engagement.
